page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is an entry-tier, memory-skewed virtual machine type hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It runs on the x86_64 architecture using an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration comprises 4 shared virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores utilizing 2 threads per core. Memory capacity is substantial relative to the compute footprint, providing 32.0 GB of system RAM, which yields 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance comes with no integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage for persistent volumes, and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Hardware acceleration is absent, with 0 GPUs provisioned.

Synthetic benchmarks demonstrate that the ecs.e4.xlarge offers constrained processing capabilities due to its shared CPU allocation model and older processor generation. In stress-ng evaluations, the single-core CPU score reached 950.58, while the multi-core result measured 3679.45. Memory throughput benchmarks show 30.12 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads and 22.11 GB/sec for uncached writes. Workload-specific metrics include a PassMark database operations score of 1128.29, Redis SET throughput of 5.32 million operations per second, and a static web serving rate of 4.72 GB/sec. Instruction set support includes AVX and AES, but lacks newer extensions such as AVX-512 and AMX, limiting compute density for vector processing and machine learning tasks.

From a qualitative cost efficiency perspective, the ecs.e4.xlarge presents an economical option for deployments needing high memory capacity without paying for dedicated compute cores. The shared CPU architecture introduces potential resource contention, meaning it is poorly suited for compute-bound production tasks or latency-critical transactions. Consequently, the instance fits workloads dominated by memory footprint rather than CPU cycles, including development environments, staging database instances, distributed memory caching nodes like Redis, internal web services, and batch jobs with light computational demands.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e4.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual instance within the shared family running on the KVM hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance allocates 4 shared vCPUs across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, offering an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The server includes no bundled local storage, relying on remote block storage, and operates with a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations indicate modest processing capacity, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 950.58 and multi-core performance reaching 3679.45, placing the CPU throughput in lower percentiles. The architecture suits memory-dependent, low-intensity tasks that benefit from higher RAM density on a shared resource model, including internal caching layers, lightweight database replicas, staging servers, and memory-oriented development environments.
